generator.params.crown_start.why: A crown a fern's rhizome branches into is part of the same plant and fed by it, so its first fronds are as large as the crown it came from; only a fern with no rhizome starts each crown from a spore.

appearance.organs.pinna.shape.template.why: A once-pinnate frond's pinnae are whole blades, drawn on a simple card along the rachis; a frond divided again (a range read at its middle, to the nearest whole number) draws each pinna on a frond card of its own pinnules. A fern whose taxa do not say is drawn divided again, as most leptosporangiate ferns are.

generator.params.arch.why: A frond's rachis bends outward over its length as it unrolls: little if it stays erect, most if it hangs.

generator.params.crowns.why: An erect rhizome bears one crown of fronds, an ascending one a crown or two, a short-creeping one a clump of a few crowns close together, a long-creeping one fronds spread far along it.

generator.params.crown_rate.why: How fast new crowns come: slowly on an ascending rhizome, faster on a short-creeping one, fast on a long-creeping one.

generator.params.rhizome.why: How far apart crowns stand: a hand's width in a clump, half a metre along a long-creeping rhizome.

generator.params.fronds_per_year.why: A crown on an erect or ascending rhizome sends up a vase of fronds each year; along a long-creeping rhizome they stand singly.

generator.params.young_angle.why: A frond rises at this angle off the vertical as it unrolls: near upright if it stays erect, more open if it spreads or hangs.

generator.params.old_angle.why: And opens to this angle as it ages.

generator.params.droop.why: And sags this much a year under its own weight: little if it is stiffly erect, most if it hangs.

generator.params.pinna_peak.why: Its longest pinnae stand where its blade's outline is widest: near its foot in a triangular blade, below the middle in a lanceolate one, above it in an oblanceolate one.

generator.params.pinna_base.why: Its lowest pinnae, as a share of the longest: nearly as long in a triangular or oblong blade, much shorter in an oblanceolate one narrowed to its foot.

generator.params.pinna_tip.why: Its topmost pinnae, as a share of the longest.

generator.params.scales.why: A stipe stated scaly is drawn with scales round it, a few if sparse, a close ring at each piece if dense, largest at its foot and smaller up it.

appearance.organs.palea.colour.why: Its scales are drawn in the colour they are stated in.

generator.params.fertile_fronds.why: A dimorphic fern's fronds are some fertile, some sterile; about three in ten of each year's are fertile.

generator.params.fertile_length.why: A fertile frond is its fertile blade and stipe, end to end.

generator.params.fertile_stipe.why: The bare share of a fertile frond is its stipe's.

generator.params.fertile_pinna_length.why: A fertile frond's longest pinnae are as long as stated, as a share of the frond.

generator.params.fertile_angle.why: A fertile frond opens to the angle its posture gives a frond.

generator.params.fertile_arch.why: And bends over its length as a frond of that posture does.

generator.params.fertile_droop.why: And sags as a frond of that posture does.

appearance.organs.fertile_pinna.shape.wi.why: A fertile pinna's card is as narrow for its length as the pinna is stated.

generator.params.scale_reach.why: Scales stated only at the stipe's base clothe its lowest three tenths, shrinking up it; scales stated along it go all the way to the blade.

generator.params.scale_length.why: The largest scales, at the stipe's foot, are as long as they are stated.

appearance.bark.why: A fern's only stems above ground are its stipes and rachises, so they are drawn in the colour its stipe is stated in.

growth.note: A fern is grown to the age most built-in ferns of the subclass are (6 years; their fronds are full size by 3 to 4).

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

appearance.note: The built-in leptosporangiate ferns' median rhizome and frond colours (2026-10-14), until a family or species states its own; every fern draws its pinnae, on the card the rule above chooses. Its scales, where its stipe is scaly, are ovate-lanceolate blades about two fifths as wide as long, red-brown (sRGB about 100, 55, 30), between the red-brown and dark brown Flora of North America gives for Polystichum munitum's (2026-10-16), until a taxon states its own. A fertile pinna, where a dimorphic fern bears fertile fronds, is a narrow simple blade an eighth as wide as long, in the leaf's colour, until a taxon states its own width (2026-10-17).

traits.sporangia.note: Ferns bear their sporangia in small clusters, sori, on the underside of their fronds (Biology 2e, 25.4). Usually rather than always, as a few ferns bear them otherwise.

traits.vernation.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923; ferns by Maxon), its account of the fern family as it then stood, which held every leptosporangiate fern of the Pacific States: blades coiled in vernation, the young frond unrolling from the tip. Usually rather than always, since a few ferns of this subclass, such as the floating water ferns, do not unroll their leaves this way.

rules.note: What the program's crown_start means: a new crown's age as a share of its parent's. Floras give a fern's fronds' sizes for the plant, not for a seedling, and describe tufted and creeping ferns as clumps or colonies of crowns of like fronds (Abrams 1923, under the sword, deer and wood ferns and bracken).

generator.program.note: The leptosporangiate ferns' own program (growth plan G2.3a): fronds that uncoil from croziers in crowns on a rhizome. Tree ferns (Cyatheaceae) grow on palm instead.

rules.generator.params.arch.note: Hoshizaki and Moran (2001, p. 391): by default fronds bend outward and droop toward the tip; most Nephrolepis are pendulous or arching, N. cordifolia stiffly erect. The degrees are the model's; the program's own default, 60, is an arching frond's.

rules.generator.params.crowns.note: Hoshizaki and Moran (2001), Fern Grower's Manual: erect stems carry their fronds in a whorl or vase-like cluster, semi-erect ones in looser whorls, and clumping rhizomes in whorls or irregular clusters (p. 13); erect or ascending rhizomes give a crown of fronds and few form several crowns (Polystichum, pp. 455, 457); on long-creeping rhizomes fronds stand singly at intervals along them (Davallia p. 265, Polypodium p. 437, Pyrrosia 2-8 cm apart p. 481). The numbers are the model's, from the curated ferns: lady, spreading wood and sword ferns (erect or ascending; one or two crowns about 0.1-0.15 m apart, 7-12 fronds a year), deer fern (short-creeping tuft) and bracken (long-creeping; 6 crowns 0.45 m apart, 1 frond a year).

rules.generator.params.young_angle.note: Hoshizaki and Moran (2001): fronds are described as erect, arching, spreading or pendent (most Nephrolepis pendulous or arching, N. cordifolia stiffly erect, p. 391). The angles and sag are the model's, the arching values those of the curated lady, wood and sword ferns (opening to 35-55 degrees, sag 0.03-0.04 a year).

rules.generator.params.old_angle.note: Hoshizaki and Moran (2001): fronds are described as erect, arching, spreading or pendent (most Nephrolepis pendulous or arching, N. cordifolia stiffly erect, p. 391). The angles and sag are the model's, the arching values those of the curated lady, wood and sword ferns (opening to 35-55 degrees, sag 0.03-0.04 a year).

rules.generator.params.droop.note: Hoshizaki and Moran (2001): fronds are described as erect, arching, spreading or pendent (most Nephrolepis pendulous or arching, N. cordifolia stiffly erect, p. 391). The angles and sag are the model's, the arching values those of the curated lady, wood and sword ferns (opening to 35-55 degrees, sag 0.03-0.04 a year).

rules.generator.params.scales.note: Flora of North America words a fern's stipe as bare, sparsely scaly or densely scaly, its scales largest at the base: Polystichum munitum's "Petiole ... densely scaly; scales red-brown to dark brown or nearly black, gradually diminishing in size distally." How many scales stand round each piece of the stipe is the model's (visual forms fern crown, 2026-10-16).

rules.appearance.organs.palea.colour.note: A stated scale colour is drawn as it is stated.

rules.generator.params.fertile_fronds.note: Flora of North America words a dimorphic fern's fertile and sterile leaves apart (Blechnum spicant: "Leaves dimorphic, cespitose, erect or spreading, fertile leaves more erect and longer than sterile leaves"). That about three in ten of a year's fronds are fertile is the model's (visual forms fern dimorphism, 2026-10-17).

rules.generator.params.fertile_length.note: As a sterile frond's length is its blade and stipe (Polypodiopsida's rule).

rules.generator.params.fertile_stipe.note: As a sterile frond's stipe share (Polypodiopsida's rule).

rules.generator.params.fertile_pinna_len.note: A stated fertile pinna length, as a share of the stated fertile frond.

rules.generator.params.fertile_angle.note: The posture words and angles of the sterile frond's rule (generator.params.old_angle), for the fertile frond's own posture.

rules.generator.params.fertile_arch.note: The posture words and bends of the sterile frond's rule (generator.params.arch), for the fertile frond's own posture.

rules.generator.params.fertile_droop.note: The posture words and sags of the sterile frond's rule (generator.params.droop), for the fertile frond's own posture.

rules.appearance.organs.fertile_pinna.sh.note: A stated fertile pinna's width over its length, drawn as its card's width over length.

rules.generator.params.scale_reach.note: Flora of North America words most ferns' petiole scales as standing at the base (Dryopteridaceae: "scales usually persistent at base"; Blechnaceae: "generally scaly at least at base"; Pteridaceae: "usually with persistent scales proximally"; Blechnum spicant: "coarsely scaly proximally"), and a few as scaly along the petiole (Polystichum munitum: "densely scaly ... gradually diminishing in size distally"). The lowest three tenths for a base is the model's (visual forms fern stipes, 2026-10-17).

rules.generator.params.scale_length.note: A stated scale length is drawn as it is stated, at the stipe's foot.

rules.appearance.bark.note: Flora of North America colours a fern's petiole, not its stem: Athyrium filix-femina's "straw-colored distally ... base dark red-brown or black", Blechnum spicant's "reddish brown". The stipe colour over most of its length is drawn on stipe and rachis alike (visual forms fern stipes, 2026-10-17).

rules.generator.params.pinna_peak.note: Hoshizaki and Moran (2001) describe blade outlines as triangular (largest pinnae at the base, as in Rumohra, p. 491), lanceolate, narrowly elliptic or oblanceolate (narrowed to the base, as in Polystichum, p. 491). Where the longest pinnae sit, and how short the lowest and topmost are, is the model's reading of each shape word's outline (the kingdom's Systematics Association outlines); the triangular value is bracken's and the spreading wood fern's.
